subsystems.name: Catalyst system
subsystems.role: provides the metal nanoparticles on which nanotubes grow.

subsystems.name: Growth reactor
subsystems.role: where carbon feedstock decomposes and nanotubes form.

subsystems.name: Fiber formation
subsystems.role: collects and twists growing nanotubes into a continuous thread.

subsystems.name: Post-processing
subsystems.role: improves alignment, packing and purity of the fiber.

subsystems.name: Composite integration
subsystems.role: binds fibers into a usable structural material.

buildSteps.title: Prepare catalyst
buildSteps.detail: Metal nanoparticles are deposited on a substrate or formed in a gas stream.

buildSteps.title: Grow nanotubes
buildSteps.detail: A carbon-containing gas enters a hot reactor, decomposes on the catalyst, and nanotubes grow.

buildSteps.title: Draw continuous fiber
buildSteps.detail: As nanotubes form, they are pulled out as an aerogel-like sock and wound onto a drum.

buildSteps.title: Purify
buildSteps.detail: Leftover catalyst and amorphous carbon are removed with heat or acid.

buildSteps.title: Align and densify
buildSteps.detail: The fiber is stretched or sheared to align nanotubes, then passed through a liquid to pack them closer.

buildSteps.title: Twist into yarn
buildSteps.detail: The densified sheet is twisted into a yarn that can be handled and woven.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into composite
buildSteps.detail: The yarn is infiltrated with polymer or metal to make a stiff, strong structural material.

buildSteps.title: Test and scale
buildSteps.detail: Tensile properties are measured, and continuous production lines are tuned for consistent output.

prerequisites.why: nanotubes cannot grow without a properly sized metal particle to seed them.
the standard method for producing carbon nanotubes at useful rates.
drawing nanotubes directly into a long thread is demonstrated but not yet reliable at scale.
individual nanotubes are strong, but a fiber is only as strong as the packing and alignment of its billions of tubes.
embedding fibers in a matrix is how they become useful structural parts.

pathway.milestone: lab-scale fibers with impressive but variable strength
pathway.unlocks: small structural parts and research into better spinning methods.

pathway.milestone: pilot-scale continuous production of consistent yarn
pathway.unlocks: commercial composites for sports goods, automotive and aerospace components.

pathway.milestone: mass production with properties approaching individual nanotubes
pathway.unlocks: ultra-light frames and cables in infrastructure and transport.
a space elevator — still theoretical and requiring strength far beyond today's fibers.
